rules.why: Recursive delete of the root or home directory.
rules.instead: Delete a specific, named subdirectory and list it first with ls.

rules.why: Destroys or changes infrastructure without a human reading the plan.
rules.instead: Run terraform plan -out=tfplan, show the plan, and let a person run apply.

rules.why: Deletes a namespace or every object of a kind.
rules.instead: Name one resource, run with --dry-run=server first, and check the current context.

rules.why: Mutating command aimed at a production context or namespace.
rules.instead: Use get/describe for read-only checks. Ask a person to run changes in prod.

rules.why: Force push can overwrite other people's commits.
rules.instead: Use git push --force-with-lease on your own branch, never on main.

rules.why: Throws away uncommitted work that cannot be recovered.
rules.instead: Run git status, then git stash or commit first.
Take and verify a backup, then ask a person to run it.

rules.why: Runs a remote script you have not read.
rules.instead: Download it, read it, then run it.
Grant the narrowest mode that works, such as 644 or 755.

rules.why: Deletes a bucket or all of its objects.
rules.instead: List the contents, check versioning and replication, and ask a person to run it.

rules.why: Prints secrets into the model's context.
rules.instead: Check that the variable is set with [ -n "$NAME" ] instead of printing it.
